content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [product_name] and have a question about handling network input with Modbus TCP. I've been trying for several days to read temperature and humidity from a combo probe that uses Modbus. I can retrieve sensor data using modpoll, so that part works. For reference: Input Register 0x0001 (2 bytes): Temperature; Input Register 0x0002 (2 bytes): Humidity. When I set up a network input block, it appears as expected but I can't use its value in the display or logic conditions. It's as if the block can't be linked to anything. I'm likely missing a step and would appreciate guidance. Best regards, [user_name]
I'm not sure why you'd describe an input register as having only bits—it probably uses 2 bytes. Could you share your program file?
Has your issue been resolved? I've previously used similar sensors and managed to connect them to [product_name] successfully.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is having difficulty linking data received from a Modbus TCP sensor in [product_name] to further logic or display options. There is uncertainty on handling Modbus input registers, and the integration with display and control logic is not clear or intuitive for the end user.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] to accept Modbus TCP input and allow direct use of these values in both display and logic blocks, without needing complicated workarounds.
pain_keywords: unable to use modbus input in logic
